question: Are the served generation's pre-kickoff forecasts sharper than the de-vigged closing 1X2 line, measured by paired RPS on the same settled fixtures?
why_now: Zero settled forecasts exist under the served identity: production /health components.settlement reported settled_predictions_total = 0 and model_version = v5_phase7-20260922@417b9b8ff7ce563d on 2026-09-26 (sha 63f9bf2). Scheduled pre-kickoff capture (L4, DEBT 157) shipped; the first scheduled captures are expected on 2026-10-09 (directive v10 §2.2). A full round across the 6 served leagues is at most 57 fixtures (EPL, LA_LIGA, SERIE_A 10 each; BUNDESLIGA, LIGUE_1, EREDIVISIE 9 each), so the first milestone of 200 settled forecasts with a close is about 4 rounds away, no earlier than the first week of November. ESTIMATE: it assumes every fixture is captured, closed and joined, and ignores international breaks. Freezing the rule now means it predates every data point it will judge.
prior: Low that the model is sharper than the close. No generation measured in this repo has shown a paired CI below zero against the de-vigged market on the 2526 holdout (0 of 6 leagues, docs/DEBT.md item 62), and the pre-registered G18 market-residual track was negative (docs/DEBT.md item 150). The close is also a harder benchmark than an opening price: it is observed at most 5 minutes before kickoff (market_observation_service._CLOSING_WINDOW_MINUTES = 5), while an L4 forecast is made about 3 hours before (prediction_capture_service.CAPTURE_WINDOW_END). 'Less sharp' or 'inconclusive' is the expected answer. The test is worth running because the rule is fixed before the data exists.

forecasts.writer: persist_prediction_log, backend/src/services/prediction_log_service.py:93. It stamps the served identity whenever the caller passes the family label v5_phase7 (lines 124-130) and sets created_at to the caller's evaluated_at, not a database insert time (line 172).
forecasts.l4_capture: capture_due_predictions, backend/src/services/prediction_capture_service.py:88, run on the five-minute CLV tick. It selects scheduled fixtures with kickoff in [now + 15 min, now + 3 h] (CAPTURE_WINDOW_START / CAPTURE_WINDOW_END, lines 43-44; query lines 102-110), so each fixture is captured once in [kickoff - 3 h, kickoff - 15 min], normally on the first tick after kickoff - 3 h. It calls get_full_analysis itself, so the stored forecast is what a user would have been served. It skips a fixture that already has any log under the served identity (_identity_has_log, line 137).
forecasts.interactive_capture: get_full_analysis, backend/src/api/endpoints/full_analysis.py:1243, passes require_scheduled_pre_kickoff=True (line 1268), so persist_prediction_log refuses a non-scheduled fixture and any evaluated_at at or after kickoff (prediction_log_service.py:132-143). Both L4 and interactive rows carry payload.capture_trigger = 'interactive_full_analysis' (full_analysis.py _shadow_log_payload).

closing_line.writer: clv_capture_service._capture_due_fixtures (backend/src/services/clv_capture_service.py:104) on the five-minute tick, for scheduled fixtures with kickoff in (now, now + 10 min] (_CAPTURE_LOOKAHEAD_MINUTES = 10, line 31; query lines 117-124). It hands The Odds API board to market_observation_service.persist_market_board.
closing_line.closing_classification: An observation is PRE_MATCH_CLOSING only if 0 < kickoff - captured_at <= 5 minutes (_classify_observation, backend/src/services/market_observation_service.py:103-117; _CLOSING_WINDOW_MINUTES = 5, line 42). At or after kickoff it is POST_KICKOFF_REJECTED. A newer close supersedes every earlier close for the fixture (is_closing_line set to False on the older rows, lines 223-240).
closing_line.bookmaker: One bookmaker per provider event, never a cross-bookmaker consensus: among the event's coherent records, the one bookmaker_preference ranks first (backend/src/providers/the_odds_api.py: Pinnacle, the sharpest book quoted, then bookmaker key order; market_observation_service.py:399). The live price a forecast records (odds_service.get_match_odds) uses the same rule, so the forecast-time price and the close are one book.
closing_line.de_vig: Proportional (multiplicative) normalisation: p_i = (1/o_i) / sum_j(1/o_j). the_odds_api.devig_probabilities, backend/src/providers/the_odds_api.py:63, called at market_observation_service.py:321 and stored as home/draw/away_implied_prob_devigged.

data.join: get_clv_records, backend/src/repositories/fixtures.py:401, via build_clv_records_query (line 272). Join key is match_id on both tables (MatchPredictionLog.match_id = MarketSnapshot.match_id = Match.id). The closing line is the latest snapshot per match with is_closing_line, coherent, captured_at < Match.match_date and all three de-vigged probabilities present (lines 291-313 and 381-389). The forecast is the latest log per match under the served identity with created_at < that closing snapshot's captured_at (line 324). Records are ordered by Match.match_date ascending (line 398). Outcome is 0/1/2 from the final score once status is in SETTLED_MATCH_STATUSES ('finished', 'completed', 'settled', 'final'; fixtures.py:17 and 442-448).

population.served_identity: v5_phase7-20260922@417b9b8ff7ce563d. This is served_identity(manifest) (backend/src/models/active_generation.py:154, hashing the fields at lines 131-137) applied to the committed backend/models/active_generation.json, verified locally on 2026-09-26, and it equals production /health components.settlement.model_version on the same day.
population.definition: Settled fixtures that have (a) a match_prediction_logs row under the served identity captured strictly before kickoff by L4 or by an interactive /full-analysis request, and (b) a strict pre-kickoff closing snapshot (is_closing_line = True, captured_at < kickoff). One forecast per fixture: the latest such log captured before the closing snapshot, as selected by get_clv_records.
population.one_identity_only: Rows under any other model_version are never pooled in (build_clv_records_query filters model_version on the forecast, fixtures.py:325 and 388). If the served generation changes before a milestone is reached, accumulation under this identity stops there and nothing from the new identity counts toward it. This follows from the frozen population; it is not a separate rule.

exclusions: a forecast captured at or after kickoff: excluded, never repaired or backfilled. Enforced at write time for /full-analysis (prediction_log_service.py:140-143) and at read time for every row (created_at < closing captured_at < kickoff, fixtures.py:310 and 324)
a fixture with no strict pre-kickoff closing snapshot: excluded from the metric and counted against the join rate
a fixture that is not settled (status not in SETTLED_MATCH_STATUSES, or a score missing): excluded (outcome None; compute_model_vs_close keeps only outcome in {0, 1, 2}, clv_service.py:84-94)
a record whose model or closing probabilities are not three finite numbers: excluded (clv_service.py:88-93)
UCL fixtures: never captured, the served generation has no UCL artifact (prediction_capture_service._supported_leagues, lines 63-71)

join_rate.definition: numerator / denominator at the same milestone cut. Numerator: fixtures in the milestone sample (population above). Denominator: settled fixtures with a forecast under the served identity captured strictly before kickoff, whether or not a close exists, i.e. the records get_settled_predictions (fixtures.py:199, query build_settled_predictions_query at line 115, created_at < match_date at line 143) returns for model_version = the served identity, cut at the same match_date.
join_rate.threshold: Reported with every result. A join rate under 80% flags the result as possibly biased: fixtures missing a close are not missing at random (Odds API quota or outage, unmatched or ambiguous team names, or the instance asleep at kickoff - 5 min, DEBT 153).
join_rate.not_computed_today: No existing function returns this ratio; the milestone run computes it from the two queries above.

primary_metric.definition: Per fixture, RPS(model) - RPS(de-vigged close), both scored against the same outcome. Negative means the model scored better.
primary_metric.rps: ranked_probability_score_rowwise, backend/src/models/evaluation/metrics.py:94: sum over classes of (cumulative predicted - cumulative observed)^2, divided by 2 (K - 1 for 3 outcomes). Outcome order home, draw, away.
primary_metric.statistic: the mean of the per-fixture differences over the milestone sample

inference.method: ISO-week cluster bootstrap 95% percentile CI: week_cluster_ci, backend/src/models/evaluation/metrics.py:395. Rows are grouped by the ISO (year, week) of Match.match_date, a naive UTC column (line 403); whole weeks are resampled with replacement (line 408); each replicate is sum(delta) / count over the resampled weeks, so weeks weigh by fixture count (line 409); the interval is np.percentile at 2.5 and 97.5 (line 410).
inference.seed_source: The directive fixes only 'a fixed seed'. 42 is proposed to match the G18 protocol (backend/scripts/research_g18_market_residual.py:202) and F3b. O8 may change it before freezing, never after.
inference.exact_call: records = await get_clv_records(session, model_version='v5_phase7-20260922@417b9b8ff7ce563d', limit=5000) with no league, started_at or ended_at; keep records exactly as compute_model_vs_close does (clv_service.py:84-94); cut to the milestone sample; y = outcomes; delta = ranked_probability_score_rowwise(y, model_probs) - ranked_probability_score_rowwise(y, closing_probs); dates = datetime.fromisoformat(match_date); result = week_cluster_ci(delta, dates, n_boot=10000, seed=42).
inference.not_the_live_endpoint: Do not read the milestone result from /model-performance or /model-performance/summary. Their model_vs_close calls compute_model_vs_close, which runs week_cluster_ci with n_boot=2000, seed=0 (clv_service.py:119), and /model-performance also windows to the last 30 days by default (performance.py:408 and 417-424).
inference.determinism: Weeks are indexed in sorted order (metrics.py:404), so the draw depends on the set of (week, delta) pairs, not on row order. The same data, replicate count and seed give the same interval.
inference.multiplicity: Three looks (200, 500, 1,000), each at an unadjusted 95% CI, as the directive specifies. No correction is applied. Under equal sharpness, the chance that at least one of three looks excludes zero is above 5%; every look is reported with its milestone number.

decision_rule.sharper_than_the_close: the CI upper bound is below 0 (week_cluster_ci field beats_market, metrics.py:416)
decision_rule.less_sharp: the CI lower bound is above 0 (field worse_than_market, metrics.py:417)
decision_rule.inconclusive: anything else, including an interval that touches 0
decision_rule.comparison: on the unrounded floats week_cluster_ci returns
decision_rule.field_names: The code's field names beats_market / worse_than_market do not change the reading. 'Sharper than the close' is a statement about forecast accuracy, not a betting edge and not closing-line value (clv_service.py docstring, lines 1-10).

reported_only.brier_decomposition: brier_score_decomposition, backend/src/models/evaluation/metrics.py:119 (Murphy three-term, n_bins = 10), model and close
reported_only.per_league_slices: mean delta and n per league; no CI is read as a finding

milestones.unit: settled forecasts with a close, as defined in population
milestones.sample_cut: Proposed (the directive does not specify a cut): at milestone N the sample is every settled joined forecast whose match_date is on or before the match_date of the N-th one in match_date order. Fixtures sharing that kickoff are included whole, never split, so n can slightly exceed N. The same cut applies to the join-rate denominator.
milestones.between_milestones: Nothing is evaluated between milestones. A weekly routine may read the settled count and notify the operator at 200, 500 or 1,000; it evaluates nothing (directive v10 §4.3). The milestone run is local, by a person.
milestones.later_milestones: Each milestone is run and reported. A later milestone does not retract an earlier one.

forbidden: refitting any model in the served generation after seeing any result
recalibrating, or changing the calibrator, after seeing any result
moving a threshold: the 0 bound, the 95% level, the 80% join-rate flag, the replicate count, the seed or the milestone counts
changing the population: the served identity, the capture window, the closing definition, the de-vig method, the bookmaker selection or the exclusions
backfill: a forecast captured at or after kickoff is excluded, never repaired
reporting a re-run with any of the above changed as C6
on_result: Whatever the answer, it is not a promotion and not a certification, and it changes neither stake_permitted nor any verdict gate. Certification remains a separate operator decision (O4). A 'sharper' result is one measured fact about one generation against one benchmark; a 'less sharp' or 'inconclusive' result is a valid, reportable outcome.

implementation_notes: 'Strictly before kickoff' is judged on created_at, which is the caller's evaluated_at (prediction_log_service.py:172), not a database clock. For L4 and /full-analysis the write also re-checks evaluated_at < kickoff under a row lock (lines 132-143).

The close is one bookmaker's price, not a market consensus. Until 2026-09-26 market capture took the key that sorted first ('betclic' before 'pinnacle') while the live price took the provider's listing order, so the benchmark could be a soft book and a different book from the forecast-time price. Both now use bookmaker_preference (Pinnacle first). This must be deployed before the first captured round (2026-10-09) and approved with the protocol (O8); after any served-identity result exists it is a forbidden population change.

Forecast lead times differ: L4 captures at about kickoff - 3 h, an interactive capture can be days earlier, and L4 skips any fixture that already has a log under the identity. The directive's population includes both, so no lead-time exclusion is applied.
Nothing here is CLV. True CLV needs the price at forecast time (payload.recommendation_market) and is not part of C6.
